### Reference: context and commands

#### `CONTEXT_FOLDER`

const · `import { CONTEXT_FOLDER } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The folder of a system that holds its context files.

```ts
const CONTEXT_FOLDER: "context";
```

#### `readContextFolder`

function · `import { readContextFolder } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Read and check a context folder: each file's header against the schema (a missing summary called out), and that
no two files share a key. `label` prefixes file names in problems (default `context`).

```ts
function readContextFolder(dir: string, label?: string): Promise<ContextFolder>;
```

#### `parseContextFile`

function · `import { parseContextFile } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Parse one context file. `file` names it in problems.

```ts
function parseContextFile(file: string, source: string): { file?: ContextFile; problems: ContextFileProblem[]; };
```

Refers to: [`ContextFileProblem`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.context-files-ts#core-contextfileproblem).

#### `ContextFile`

interface · `import { ContextFile } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

One checked context file.

```ts
interface ContextFile {
  /** Its path, relative to the folder it was read from, with forward slashes. */
  readonly file: string;
  /** Its whole text, so later checks can point at a line. */
  readonly source: string;
  readonly header: ContextFileHeader;
  /** What it becomes in the manifest: the header, `key` as the name, and the body as the content. */
  readonly decl: ContextDecl;
  /** The 1-based line its body starts on. */
  readonly bodyLine: number;
}
```

Refers to: [`ContextDecl`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.contextdecl#core-contextdecl), [`ContextFileHeader`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.context-files-ts#core-contextfileheader).

function · `import { contextChange } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

#### `watchContextFolder`

function · `import { watchContextFolder } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Watch a context folder (dev) and send each settled change as a runtime patch, by key. `initial` is what the system
started with. One rescan runs at a time (a change during one rescans again after it), so patches reach the hub in
order; what the hub has only moves on once a patch is sent, and a failed one is tried again with backoff, so no
change is lost. Returns a stop function.

```ts
function watchContextFolder(dir: string, initial: readonly ContextDecl[], send: (change: SystemPatch) => Promise<unknown>, options: ContextWatchOptions): () => void;
```

Refers to: [`ContextDecl`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.contextdecl#core-contextdecl).

#### `ContextWatchEvents`

interface · `import { ContextWatchEvents } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What `watchContextFolder` reports.

```ts
interface ContextWatchEvents {
  /** The folder has problems; nothing was sent until they are fixed. */
  problems(problems: readonly ContextFileProblem[]): void;
  /** A change went to the hub. */
  sent(change: SystemPatch): void;
  /** Reading or sending a change failed; it is tried again. */
  failed(error: unknown): void;
}
```

Refers to: [`ContextFileProblem`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.context-files-ts#core-contextfileproblem).

#### `ContextWatchOptions`

interface · `import { ContextWatchOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `watchContextFolder` waits: for the folder to settle, and between tries when sending fails.

```ts
interface ContextWatchOptions {
  /** How long the folder must be quiet before it is read. */
  readonly debounce: number;
  /** The first wait before sending a failed change again; it doubles up to `retryMax`. */
  readonly retry: number;
  readonly retryMax: number;
  /** Prefixes file names in problems (default `context`). */
  readonly label?: string;
  readonly events: ContextWatchEvents;
}
```

#### `context`

function · `import { context } from '@harness/sdk'`

Declare static context.

```ts
/** Declare static context. */
function context<const Args extends Record<string, ArgDef<boolean>> = {}>(def: ContextInput<Args> & { content: string; }): ContextDef<ArgsOf<Args>, false>;
/** Declare dynamic context: the server implements it. */
function context<const Args extends Record<string, ArgDef<boolean>> = {}>(def: ContextInput<Args>): ContextDef<ArgsOf<Args>, true>;
```

#### `ContextInput`

interface · `import { ContextInput } from '@harness/sdk'`

What `context()` takes.

```ts
interface ContextInput<Args extends Record<string, ArgDef<boolean>>> {
  description: string;
  /** What people (and the injected section's heading) call it; its description when absent. */
  title?: string;
  /** Makes it a `/name` command. Args fill `{{name}}` in the content (or are passed to a dynamic implementation). */
  command?: { name: string; args?: Args };
  imports?: AnyContextRef[];
  fns?: AnyFnRef[];
  suggestFns?: AnyFnRef[];
  suggest?: Audience;
  visible?: Audience;
  /** Put it in these agents' system prompts (`{ into: [agents.startingWith(hub.fns.chat)], order: 40 }`). Its `fns` join their starting tools. */
  inject?: InjectInput;
  tags?: string[];
  /** How much it counts when scored, from 0 (left out) to 2. Default 1. */
  weight?: number;
  /** A short form shown when the budget allows only a little of it. */
  summary?: string;
  parent?: AnyContextRef;
  next?: AnyContextRef;
  /** Weighted links to other context, fns, types and resources. */
  links?: ContextLinkDef[];
}
```

Refers to: [`Audience`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-audience).

#### `ContextDef`

interface · `import { ContextDef } from '@harness/sdk'`

Content for the LLM. Static content is written in the contract; dynamic content is produced by the system.

```ts
interface ContextDef<A, Dynamic extends boolean> {
  readonly description: string;
  /** What people (and the injected section's heading) call it; its description when absent. */
  readonly title: string | undefined;
  readonly dynamic: Dynamic;
  readonly content: string | undefined;
  readonly command: { readonly name: string; readonly args: Readonly<Record<string, ArgDef<boolean>>> } | undefined;
  readonly imports: readonly AnyContextRef[];
  readonly fns: readonly AnyFnRef[];
  readonly suggestFns: readonly AnyFnRef[];
  /** Who it may be suggested to. Default `both`. */
  readonly suggest: Audience;
  /** Who can find it in searches. Default `both`. */
  readonly visible: Audience;
  /** Put it in these agents' system prompts; its `fns` join their starting tools. */
  readonly inject: InjectInput | undefined;
  readonly tags: readonly string[];
  /** How much it counts when the graph contextor scores it: 0 leaves it out, 2 doubles it. Default 1. */
  readonly weight: number | undefined;
  /** A short form shown when the budget allows only a little of it; its description otherwise. */
  readonly summary: string | undefined;
  /** Its parent in a hierarchy (a guide over its chapters). */
  readonly parent: AnyContextRef | undefined;
  /** The next piece of a chain (a long text in ordered pieces). */
  readonly next: AnyContextRef | undefined;
  readonly links: readonly ContextLinkDef[];
  /** Phantom: the command's args. Never set at runtime. */
  readonly argsType?: A;
}
```

Refers to: [`Audience`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-audience).

#### `ContextLinkDef`

interface · `import { ContextLinkDef } from '@harness/sdk'`

A weighted edge from a context item to something it relates to, which the graph contextor follows: `imports` and
`brings` travel together; `suggests`, `related`, `about`, `parent` and `next` pass on some of an item's score.

```ts
interface ContextLinkDef {
  readonly to: ContextLinkTarget;
  readonly relation: DeclarableRelation;
  /** How strongly, from 0 to 1. Default 0.5. */
  readonly weight?: number;
}
```

Refers to: [`DeclarableRelation`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.context-graph-ts#core-declarablerelation).

interface · `import { ContextRef } from '@harness/sdk'`

A typed handle to context. A `/command`'s args are typed. In a template string it writes `context:<its key>`, rendered as the key.

#### `InjectInput`

interface · `import { InjectInput } from '@harness/sdk'`

Where an item of context is injected: the system prompts of the agents it targets, in their `{{injectedContext}}`
section. It waits for an admin's approval like any change to the system's contract, and an admin can switch it off
for any agent.

```ts
interface InjectInput {
  /** The agents it goes into: refs and patterns (`agents.startingWith(hub.fns.chat)`, `'crm/*'`). At least one. */
  readonly into: readonly [AgentTarget, ...AgentTarget[]];
  /** Lower comes first. Default 100; the hub's own items are 10 to 30. */
  readonly order?: number;
  /** Fns its text names without bringing them: it is left out unless they can be used. Its `fns` are required too. */
  readonly requires?: readonly AnyFnRef[];
  /** Only in this chat mode. Leave it out unless the text is true in one mode only. */
  readonly mode?: 'tools' | 'static';
  /**
   * Context items it takes the place of, as refs (`[hub.context.later]`; a name as a string doesn't compile): while
   * it goes into an agent's section, each is left out of that section (`replaced`), so the item says what is true
   * instead. When it is out (its system off, switched off), they are back. Restate what the replaced item says that
   * is still true.
   */
  readonly replaces?: readonly AnyContextRef[];
}
```

#### `AgentTarget`

type · `import { AgentTarget } from '@harness/sdk'`

One entry of `inject.into`: an agent's ref (`hub.fns.chat`; only `hub/llm` fns fit), or a pattern.

```ts
type AgentTarget = AgentRef | AgentPattern;
```

#### `AgentPattern`

type · `import { AgentPattern } from '@harness/sdk'`

Agents by a pattern over their qualified names. `*` alone is every agent; any other pattern is `system/local`, where
each `*` stands for any run of characters (none included) on its own side of the `/`: it crosses `.`, never `/`.
Case counts, and `**` is refused. A string without `*` doesn't compile: one agent is named by its ref.

```ts
type AgentPattern = '*' | `${string}*${string}/${string}` | `${string}/${string}*${string}`;
```

#### `agents`

const · `import { agents } from '@harness/sdk'`

Patterns built from refs, so renaming an agent or a system breaks the build instead of the match.

```ts
const agents: { readonly all: "*"; readonly of: <const S extends string>(system: { readonly name: S extends `${string}/${string}` ? never : S; }) => `${S}/*`; readonly startingWith: <const N extends QualifiedName>(agent: AgentRef<N>) => `${N}*`; };
```

Refers to: [`QualifiedName`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-qualifiedname).
